text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:
- The number of unemployed persons in Switzerland rose to 183,026 or 5.1 percent in November. The percentage of young adults aged 20 - 24 increased by 7.2 percent.
- Some 6,000 calves were slaughtered in Switzerland because they were found to have illegally high levels of antibiotics.
- Switzerland's Federal Department of Health okayed the marketing of food containing genetically altered soy beans. The use of vitamin B-12 produced with genetic technology was also approved.
- Swiss watchdog Federal Banking Commission elected two more women as members.
- Swiss Ambassador Thomas Borer said on Swiss radio that he is not sure whether statements made by the Jewish World Congress regarding Nazi gold and Holocaust victims' funds were always true.
- The Toni Group, Switzerland's largest milk product producer, confirmed that it will continue to restructure and cut down overcapacity in 1997.
- Watchmaker Baume & Mercier is reducing its line of products and modernising its communications.
